title: The Answer Was on Top
thesis_this_serves: An answer that repeats for every searcher sat on top of a stack of summaries, and the one binding text was underneath. The look has to make DEPTH the argument: top is bright and easy, bottom is dark and binding, and the camera earns the descent.

roles.sky: #A9B7C0  Kodiak slate fog, cold blue-grey overcast, the marsh at 7am
roles.ground: #2B211A  wet peat umber, the binder and the marsh floor, the dark anchor
roles.hero: #E8590C  hunter orange, ONE MEANING ONLY: the repeated wrong answer (the answer card and its twin). It never marks the binder
roles.accent: #8C9A86  lichen grey-green, desaturated sedge on the marsh and the tag's corrected state
roles.paper: #ECEEEA  cool grey-white summary stock, never warm bone

palette.mood: Cold, quiet, damp and fair. Nobody is scolded. The only warm thing in a slate world is the wrong answer, so orange reads as a warning without a red alarm, and when the tag reaches the binder it turns cream on peat so the move reads as the answer being corrected, never as the binder being marked wrong.
palette.divergence: Measured against the last ten films. 2026-09-23 was dusk violet #3E3852, birch gold #C9A227, copper #C87137 and carbon #1F3A5F. 2026-09-19 was powerhouse green with sodium amber and cyan. 2026-08-05 was cabinet green #1E332C, bone #EDE7DA and brass #C9963F. This film has no green ground, no violet, no gold, no brass, no copper, no cyan, and no warm-bone paper: slate fog #A9B7C0, peat umber #2B211A, cool paper #ECEEEA. Its only warm role is hunter orange, which none of the last ten used as a hero role. Orange has one semantic job.

light.time_of_day: 07:10, September 5th and after, Kodiak. Sun not yet over the ridge, then indoor lamp and phone glow for the rest.
light.direction: soft overcast from above for the marsh; a single warm lamp from frame RIGHT on the kitchen table; the phone glass lights hands from below
light.key: per setup, see setups; nothing else is lit by an unnamed source
light.rim: cream rim on the top edge of every sheet, so the stack reads as real bodies with thickness
light.depth_approach: FIVE summary sheets plus one binder, seen at a declared 3/4 oblique camera (yaw 18 degrees, pitch 24 degrees) so thickness reads. Per-plane table: plane 1 (top, the answer sheet) fill #ECEEEA L93 blur 0 rim 1.0 shadow +6/+10; plane 2 #DCE0E1 L88 blur 0.6 rim 0.8 shadow +5/+8; plane 3 #C8CED1 L82 blur 1.4 rim 0.6; plane 4 #B0B8BD L74 blur 2.4 rim 0.45; plane 5 #939DA3 L64 blur 3.6 rim 0.3; binder #2B211A L15 blur 0 (always in focus) rim 0.15 with a hard 1px contact shadow, rounded spine, stitched head band and a visible page-block edge. Sheets are only 8 to 12 percent translucent over a cream underlay so the binder never bleeds through. Exterior table: far ridge #8797A1 at 18 percent contrast, mid marsh #6F7C6C at 100, near alder #2B211A at 130 with slight blur.

setups.kitchen (S3): key warm lamp from frame RIGHT (a lamp pool #D9B37A at 30 percent, the only warm source), fill slate, rim cream on hands
setups.phone/cab (S1,S5,S13): key screen glow from below via screenlight.tsx ScreenLit/ScreenKey, fill fog, rim none

shape_language.grammar: THE THIN, LIGHT SUMMARY AGAINST THE THICK, DARK BINDING TEXT.
shape_language.why_this_story: The argument is about layers. So every summary is a thin translucent pale rectangle that floats and wobbles, and the binding regulation is a thick, matte, spruce-dark block with a spine and page edge, heavy and still. Natural forms (marsh grass, fog, snipe silhouettes) are irregular. The stack never blends with them, it lies over the land like a document does.
shape_language.the_deliberate_contrast: Thin pale floaty rectangles against one thick dark still block. Not a document layout: the camera travels through the sheets like a core sample.
shape_language.binder_wins_at_feed_scale: The binder carries a SECOND contrast axis beyond value: a rounded spine, a stitched head band, a page-block edge and a hard contact shadow, all at the 3/4 camera tilt, where sheets get only a soft float shadow. A 0.28-scale legibility strip is run on S11 before any other scene is authored.

casting.hero_reason: The story's real subject is the one thick still text underneath, and no bound thick block exists on the shelf. NET-NEW in lib/stack.tsx: Binder (thick spruce-dark... peat umber, spine, head band, page-block edge, contact shadow, opens via peel 0..1 to a printed page), DateTag (the orange throughline tab with a state param orange/cream and an engraving), AnswerCard (the orange card and its lockstep twin). The stack of summaries is a THIN composite explicitly built on evidence.tsx FrameStack plus paper.tsx Sheet: it is not the net-new hero. Hero differs from the last two, Statement and RunOfRiver.
from_the_shelf: paper.tsx Sheet and PaperFiber for every summary sheet and the affidavit
evidence.tsx FrameStack as the base of the summary stack (extended with ladder, blur and wobble params, registered as an upgrade)
props.tsx GripHand for the hand silhouettes
absence.tsx Unnamed for the GOOGLE DID NOT RESPOND slot, with its required label
screenlight.tsx ScreenLit/ScreenKey for the phone shots
casting.cast_freshness: hero Binder differs from the last two heroes.

motion_language.how_the_world_moves: Everything thin wobbles on a spring. The binder is still. The camera descends through the stack and makes exactly one licensed upward move, the S11 pull-back.
key_hero_moves: the orange answer card slams onto the phone glass with overshoot at 0.5s
the twin card clacks down in perfect sync with the first, a mirrored bounce
the DateTag is torn off the top sheet and slides to the bottom of the stack
the peel: a hand lifts the summaries away one by one with DocumentFlip until it reaches the binder
motion_language.blur_anticipation: 180 degree shutter on the slam and the peel; anticipation of about 3 frames before every stamp

composition.staging: 9:16 master graded; the square is derived at y 420 to 1500. Story band 500 to 1300, captions own 1336 to 1472. Sheets fill above and below the crop.
composition.focal_hierarchy: one card or tag at frame center at every key moment; the stack is the background structure
composition.negative_space: fog above the marsh; black phone glass in the hook
composition.signature_shot: S11: the camera, which has only descended until now, licenses ONE upward move, a pull-back that reveals the whole tower of five summaries on the one thick still binder, with the tag torn off the top and sliding down to rest on the binder as cream on peat. The pull-back is the payoff of the descent and the single exception to 'the camera only goes down'.

craft_advance.how: lib/focus.tsx: blurAt(z, focusZ, aperture) and valueLadder(z, planes) pure functions with a test seam, so any Stage3D or stacked scene derives per-plane blur and value from its Z distance to the focal plane instead of hand-set blur. Used by the stack here. Registered under Engine systems in ASSET_MANIFEST.md.

fingerprint.note: 09-14 and earlier descents were orbital-aerial or instrument-as-subject; this one is a cross-section core sample at a 3/4 oblique camera.

dead_space_guard: Legibility strip at 0.28 scale for S8 and S11 before authoring.
